llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The broad trigger terms are real but only affect when the documentation may be surfaced; the artifact does not itself perform actions or hide unrelated behavior.
[SQP-2] expected: Messaging, instance management, group changes, QR retrieval, and webhook configuration are disclosed in the summary and endpoint reference, though stronger safety guidance would be useful.
[SQP-2] expected: Webhook and WebSocket forwarding is purpose-aligned and documented with user-supplied endpoints, but operators should treat forwarded conversation events as sensitive data.
llm.guidance: Install only if you intend to connect an agent to a real P-API/WhatsApp environment. Use a limited API key where possible, verify recipients and message content before sending, require explicit approval for deletion or group changes, and configure only trusted HTTPS/WSS webhook destinations that can safely handle private message data.
llm.summary: This is a documentation-only WhatsApp API skill whose powerful messaging and management capabilities are disclosed and aligned with its purpose, but users should operate it carefully.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: p-api
Version: 1.2.1

The skill bundle describes a WhatsApp automation API, detailing its features, configuration, authentication, and various endpoints for sending messages, managing instances, groups, product catalogs, and integrations (Typebot, Chatwoot, webhooks, WebSockets). All content, including the SKILL.md instructions, is purely descriptive and instructional for using the API, without any evidence of prompt injection attempts against the AI agent, data exfiltration, malicious execution, persistence, or obfuscation. The external domains (papi.api.br, mundoautomatik.com) are presented as official links for the service and its partner, not for malicious purposes.
